obligations.residual_obligations: AARM deferral ordering, cascade bounds and follow-up receipts require deployment-specific work. ECL hold and timeout-to-safe-state are different mechanisms; TS1-009 does not supply a session deferral scheduler.
assumptions: The runtime boundaries and action classes are declared; no undisclosed bypass is available.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: ECL supplies workflow and digest-bound causal linkage, not a session-context store, accumulated data classification, original-intent store or rolling context hash log; those stay with other tools by design. Their outputs connect as decision inputs that the register classifies (ECL1N-0178) and that the decision record identifies by reference and digest (ECL1N-0181); a classification made by a model is a judgment input.
assumptions: Causal linkage is supporting evidence; it is not accumulated context provided to a policy engine.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: The deployment must implement the external action classifications, predicate conflict resolution and parameter policies. AuthZEN supplies a policy-engine interface, not those policies.
assumptions: Native enforcement still applies even when an external policy engine permits.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: ECL does not evaluate accumulated intent; intent alignment stays with other tools by design. An intent-alignment or confidence result connects as a judgment input that can hold, deny or challenge an action but never admit it (ECL1N-0179, DCMP2-053), and missing context maps to an unavailable required input, which prevents an admit (ECL1N-0182). Equal-priority conflict deferral remains deployment policy.
assumptions: Hold and challenge carry a disposition; they do not implement contextual intent analysis.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: Admit/deny map directly; challenge and hold are approximate STEP_UP/DEFER analogues with different continuation and timeout semantics. ECL has no MODIFY parameter-transformation outcome, approval router or cascading-deferral scheduler; an AARM deployment's MODIFY and deferral connect to ECL decisions through the binding profile AARM-BINDING-1 in profiles/.
assumptions: Outcome vocabulary similarity is not wire, behavior or conformance equivalence.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: Deployments must supply all AARM receipt context, approvals and deferral fields, among them an accumulated-context store and the AARM five-disposition receipts, which ECL-1 does not specify. Signature validity alone does not prove execution truth or assessment independence.
assumptions: Signed canonical evidence and caller-selected trust material support offline checking; corroboration is labeled at its actual evidence level.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: Human, service, agent, session and role claims need a deployment identity source, freshness and revocation checks. FR-106 addresses opaque secret handles, not identity validation; attestation and rotation are normative obligations that each deployment meets.
assumptions: Actor/subject separation and attenuated authority scope support binding; scope is not a role-directory or identity-provider implementation.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: Embedding-based and cumulative semantic drift detection, calibration and alerts are not ECL surfaces; they stay with other tools by design. A drift detector connects as a judgment input that can only make a decision stricter (ECL1N-0179), or as a declared detection whose response holds or stops the affected actions (ECL1N-0167, ECL1N-0168).
assumptions: This is a recommended AARM obligation; absence does not become ECL drift-detection support.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: Evidence retention and export are not real-time OCSF/CEF/custom SIEM telemetry streaming, filtering or batching. Telemetry and SIEM tools stay outside ECL by design and consume exported ECL evidence through the profile OTEL-EVIDENCE-EXPORT-1 in profiles/.
assumptions: No SIEM export implementation or streaming latency is claimed.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.

obligations.residual_obligations: Bounded authority and delegation attenuation do not issue just-in-time credentials. Credential provisioning, scoping and usage logging remain deployment work.
assumptions: The profile requires attested, rotated workload identity and a 24-hour static-secret cap; those requirements do not establish a running credential service.
Classification identifies the cited ECL support; it does not establish satisfaction of the entire external clause. Deployment evidence remains necessary.
